exact_edit_check.description: Relative to the pre-qualification executor, only roll_free expression and explanatory comments changed. Prior raw-valid/mode qualification was removed. No recipe source was edited by this candidate.

checks.name: same-edge completion and different idle-slot issue
checks.result: Retirement still clears pipe_active[pipe_tag], increments pipe_completed and writes the endpoint using the old per-slot chain index. If another slot was already idle, pipe_selected can still accept there on the same edge. Because the selected slot was idle and the retired slot active, they cannot alias under legal ownership.

checks.name: all slots active
checks.result: roll_free is zero so pipe_selected is false. A valid completion clears its slot on that edge. The slot becomes eligible the following cycle. Final completion can still exit PIPE_ISSUE immediately via the unchanged pipe_valid/completed check.

checks.name: tag ownership and pending intake
checks.result: pipe_active is set on the outer accepted batch request, covering both pending and running recipe contexts. It clears only on the corresponding rolling response. No selected slot overlaps a pending/running context. Recipe busy/pending/retire admission remains unchanged as an additional guard.

checks.name: stall and ordering
checks.result: When ready or work is absent, no issue occurs and pipe_next_chain/prefetch do not advance. Different slot choice can change completion order, but each accepted slot records pipe_chain_index and writes back by that recorded index.

checks.name: P1
checks.result: pipe_direct requires PIPELINE>1, so P1 never enables rolling; its scalar execution path and cycles are structurally unaffected.

checks.name: capture behavior
checks.result: Rolling is enabled only for pipe_direct and not (macro_flags[0] && leaf_cursor==target). pipe_direct excludes indexing==1 FORS and all Verify modes. Therefore a rolling chain cannot have batch_capture_enable asserted. Capture batches retain their old nonrolling slot issue/order/readout path. No capture RAM or response consumption logic changed.

checks.name: latency scope
checks.result: Only immediate reuse of the just-completed rolling slot is delayed to the next cycle. Existing idle-slot refill remains available. Nonrolling, FORS/L-tree fixed batches and P1 are structurally unchanged; actual full-job cycle changes require RTL simulation.

abstract_model.type: Exhaustive finite one-edge scheduling model for P<=12; selected boundary vectors for P24. Not sequential RTL formal verification.
assumptions: A retirement tag owns an active slot.
The modeled edge is within active rolling batch mode.
work and ready are independent Boolean inputs.
Reset, entering/exiting rolling mode and recipe internals are reviewed separately in source; not modeled as a transition system.
abstract_model.transition: free=~active within P bits; issue=work && ready && any(free); slot=lowest free bit; next_active=(active minus retired bit) plus issued bit.
properties: No issue into a previously active slot
Retire and issue tags differ if both occur
Active count changes by issue minus retire
Existing idle slots permit issue despite a simultaneous completion
All-active completion becomes eligible next cycle
No issue when no work or not ready

structural_effect.note: This is a local scheduling fact, not a proved additive upper bound on whole-job runtime.

not_performed: No RTL simulation run by this reviewer
No claim of measured timing/area benefit
